approach: Add `check_root_cause_diagnosis(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and register it as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_code_survey`. It applies when the reading has a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, at least one behavior criterion, and the request's PROSE (its non-bullet lines) has a bug-fix word. It then requires (a) a root-cause criterion that says 'root cause', says where the wrong output enters or why it is not excluded, and names a concrete location (a crates/ path or a backticked identifier or data source), and (b) a behavior criterion that names a test (backticked identifier, path or `cargo test`) and says it fails on the base tree or without the change. A criterion that equals one of the request's own bullets (normalised, marker stripped) never counts, so copying the stock bullets 'The root cause is named ... where it originates' and 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' is refused. Add `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` and a seventh `READING_RULES` line in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Add unit tests, corpus cases, a CHANGELOG Fixed entry and a short docs/architecture.md paragraph. The gate reads only the reading and request, never the repository. Prompt files, records and the decisions page are untouched. The 8% share is declared (so the replay hold reads it) and labelled an estimate.

decisions.choice: Fix it at the reading gate with a new `check_*` step in `refusing_check`, not in the decisions page code.
decisions.reason: Both rejected jobs (20261103-201526-t4qv, 20261103-231808-3gkq) moved a filter because the accepted reading never required a diagnosis or a test that fails on the base. The gate is where that reading was accepted. `refusing_check` is the single entry point and refusal_corpus.rs enforces one refusing case per step.

rejected.why: That is one instance; out of scope and the candidates are dropped.
The mechanism default requires a refusal, not prose alone.

decisions.choice: Detect a bug-fix job from the request's prose only: non-bullet lines (lines for which `is_bullet`, reading.rs:2390, is false), lowercased with `_` turned into `x` as `check_governance_coverage` does, matched as whole words with `has_phrase` (reading.rs:3366). Words: fix, fixes, fixed, fixing, bug, bugs, wrong, broken, regression, and the phrase 'still shows'. 'already', 'fails' and 'failing' are NOT triggers by themselves.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Acceptance bullets of feature requests often say 'fails with a clear message when ...' or 'already exists'; those words in bullets or alone are ordinary. Standalone 'already' or 'fails' alongside a symptom word would add nothing, since the symptom word triggers anyway, so they are dropped. The example request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it' is still caught by 'fix'. Whole-word matching leaves 'prefix', 'fixture' and `fix_x` alone. A continuation line of a wrapped bullet counts as prose; this limit is accepted and noted in the doc comment.

rejected.option: Match the whole request text including bullets
rejected.why: Feature bullets with 'fails when' would be refused (finding 2).

rejected.option: Count 'fails'/'already' only together with a symptom word
rejected.why: Redundant: the symptom word already triggers.
Changes the closed class list and config; the reader could pick another class and bypass it.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must (1) contain 'root cause' or 'root-cause', (2) contain a locator stem (where, enter, originat, why, exclud, because), (3) name a concrete location: `names_crates_path` (reading.rs:3454) or a backticked code span, and (4) not equal any request bullet after normalising (`normalised`, reading.rs:3906, with the leading `- `, `* ` or `N. ` removed). The test criterion must be kind Behavior, contain 'test', contain fail/fails/failing as a whole word, contain a base phrase ('base tree', 'base commit', 'on the base', 'without the change', 'without the fix', 'before the change'), name a test (a backticked span, a crates/ path or 'cargo test'), and not equal a request bullet.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The stock bullets every root-cause request carries (refusal_corpus.rs:227-228) have no path or backticked name, and equal a request bullet, so copying them fails twice over. A generic 'root cause ... where ... originates' sentence with no location also fails. This requires the reader to say where the wrong items enter, which is what introspection 20261104-054700-e6js asked for. Whether the test uses real approved and rejected data cannot be decided from text; the guide asks for it and the doc comment marks it prose-only.

rejected.option: Accept any criterion with 'root cause' plus a locator word

rejected.why: Reader writes free text; a template refuses good readings.

rejected.option: Mechanically require real recorded data in the test criterion
rejected.why: Not decidable from text without false refusals.

decisions.choice: Put guidance in a new `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` constant plus a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs, and raise the section-size bound in the brief test. The guide says: write a root-cause criterion that names the file, function or data source where the wrong items enter and why they are not excluded, in your own words, not the request's bullet; and a behavior criterion that names a test, built from real recorded data of both kinds (approved and rejected), that fails on the base tree and passes with the change.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks for a constant composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Every reading check has a rule line (briefs.rs test near 3965), so a new check without one would drift. The reader prompt set is 1997 of 2000 tokens and the verifier set 1298 of 1300 (docs/system-facts.md), and the briefs sit outside those sets, so no prompt file changes.

rejected.why: No token headroom; out of scope.
The criterion asks for a separate constant.

decisions.choice: Declare the share in the check's doc comment, the CHANGELOG entry and a `replay_declaration` unit test using the exact phrase 'expected 8% of newly refused readings', followed in each place by 'This share is an estimate; the snapshot has no records, so no replay was run when it was written.'
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. `replay_is_held` holds a job whose newly refused share exceeds the declared share plus the margin, so the declaration must exist; the figure is honestly labelled an estimate. Narrowing detection to prose and to symptom words (decision 2) lowers the chance that the real share exceeds it. The estimate's phrase must stay exactly parseable by `declared_percent` (reading.rs:3917), so the estimate caveat is a separate sentence.

rejected.why: The replay would hold the job at 10% with no recorded intent.

decisions.choice: Add a unit test that builds this job's own reading shape (its request prose with 'Fix', class code, the brief's criteria 1 and 4 as written) and asserts `check_reading_acceptance` accepts it.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4: a retry or re-read of this job runs through the new gate. Criterion 4 of the brief names the root cause with `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`; criterion 1 is a behavior criterion that names a `cargo test` command and says it 'fails on the base tree'.

rejected.option: No check of the job's own reading
rejected.why: A gate that refuses its own job's reading would stall a retry.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks, each as its own command, on the final tree. The full test run covers athena-core, athena-context, the corpus, `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` and the xtask policy tests (boundary words, crate graph parse of docs/architecture.md).
demonstrations.observes: Exit 0 for `cargo fmt --all --check`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, then `cargo test --locked`. New text uses no banned word or email-like string.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting slip, an unused helper or a clippy lint fails the first two; an existing test moved by the seventh rule line or the 2400 bound fails the third.
demonstrations.seam: Cargo commands on the whole workspace; no double.
